The larval abdomen has eight pairs of lateral filaments with cottony gill tufts at their bases, and terminal hooked appendages help resist stream current.
Insect biological gills allow dissolved oxygen to diffuse into the body and are usually outgrowths of the tracheal system; the internal breathing diagram is generalized.
Aquatic larvae live beneath rocks or logs in streams and prey on aquatic animals.

Male mandibles are long and sickle-shaped; female mandibles are much shorter.
Adults can exceed 3.5 inches in length and larvae are approximately 2–3 inches long.
